A post-tensile-test heat treatment of 373 K for 90 h was applied to some workpieces to recover only the Cottrell atmosphere (diffusion of C in the Fe matrix) while keeping dislocations stationary; the condition was calculated from the average diffusion distance X = (2Dt)^(1/2). This defines a separate heat-treated condition, not the as-deformed after-25% sample.

Table 1 (specimens A–E: as received, with 15% pre-strain, heat-treated after 15% pre-strain, heat-treated after received, annealed), Table 2, and Fig. 4 concern a different material, SPCC sheet of 1.2 mm thickness with 15% pre-strain, and are excluded from the SPCE after-25%-deformation sample.

The paper attributes the decrease of the elastic modulus after plastic deformation to three reasons: increase of residual stress (which disturbs elastic recovery), increase of micro-cracks (which decrease density; the density reduction due to plastic deformation is less than 1%), and variation in the dislocation structure (movable/piled-up dislocations).

In mild steel, dislocations may be locked by carbon and other solutes (Cottrell effect) before plastic deformation; during plastic deformation they are released and move with lower internal stress, and the Cottrell atmosphere is not recovered at room temperature because the diffusion rate of C in the Fe matrix is very low.
